sections.h2: Women are under a quarter of India's registered investors

chart.title: Women's share runs from 15.7% in Bihar to 29% in Maharashtra
chart.sub: Women as a share of registered individual investors, %.
chart.source: NSE investor data, FY25 and FY26, as reported.

sections.means: Women were 24.9% of registered individual investors nationally in FY26, with Uttar Pradesh and Bihar well below that.
sections.todo: Close the entry gap in lagging states, starting with Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.

sections.h2: Once invested, women put in more per transaction than men

chart.title: Women's average lump sums run 45% higher and SIP tickets 22% higher
chart.sub: Women's average investment compared with men's, % higher.
chart.source: NSE and mutual-fund industry data, as cited in the post.

sections.means: Women who invest hold larger tickets than men, so the gap lies in how many women enter the market, not in their conviction once in.
sections.todo: Make the first entry step easy for women, since that is where the gap sits.

sections.h2: Demat accounts reached about 234 million, with 30 million added each year

chart.title: Demat accounts rose from about 150 million in March 2025 to 234 million in July 2026
chart.source: NSE, as cited in the post.

sections.means: Zero-brokerage trades, SIPs starting at ₹100–500 and UPI-linked funding have lowered the cost of starting.
sections.todo: Use these low entry costs to bring more women into equity and mutual-fund investing, not leveraged currency trading.
